items.notes: Original WSJ report paywalled; no PAHO statement found yet, hence Reported.
items.text: The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the United States' measles-elimination status, held since 2000, after more than 12 months of continuous transmission, the Wall Street Journal first reported. More than 5,400 cases have been confirmed this year, over double 2025, and states report 10 measles-associated deaths (two more on Nov 13); the CDC lists six. Al Jazeera reports HHS Secretary Kennedy asked the CDC not to count the deaths, saying there is no evidence they were measles-associated.

SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage (Ship 42) with the launch-tower arms for the first time at Starbase on Nov 14, about 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off; the ship had deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The planned double catch failed when the Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf splashdown after a low-fuel alarm. SpaceX calls ship recovery the missing step toward full reuse.

items.notes: Senate projection is FairVote analysis, not an official tabulation; official RCV count still due.
items.text: AP and CNN projected Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins the winner of the Alaska governor's race with 50.7% of first choices. In the Senate race, FairVote's preliminary ranked-choice tally from the Nov 13 cast-vote record has Mary Peltola beating Sen. Dan Sullivan 51.5% to 48.5% (about 8,000 votes), with roughly 11,000 ballots outstanding; no major outlet had called it.

Reuters, citing three people familiar with the talks, reported that Trump has told advisers he may refrain from new strikes on Iran unless Tehran or the Houthis provoke fresh action; a third carrier is still heading to the region. Separately, Israel Hayom reported, unconfirmed, that Mossad warned the CIA of an Iranian drone plot against Trump and senior officials.

Ahead of Trump's Asia trip, the CS Monitor reports he attends ASEAN in Manila on Tuesday with a Marcos bilateral and a Quad leaders' summit, then APEC in Shenzhen with a Xi meeting. A Trump–Putin–Xi trilateral is reported to be in the works but not confirmed; the White House is playing down expectations.

items.notes: Headline-level; article not read in full.
items.text: CNBC reports heating-oil prices are up about 59% on last winter as the Iran war keeps distillate supply tight, squeezing Northeast households.

items.notes: Party pledges; costs not given. Leaving the ETS would require leaving or breaching EU law — not addressed by speakers.
items.text: At an economic convention in Katowice, PiS set out a programme: Czarnek promised a lower health contribution for entrepreneurs earning up to 120,000 zł, raising the second PIT threshold from 120,000 to 180,000 zł, tax relief for working pensioners, the return of the tax card, and leaving the EU ETS at once to cut power and heat prices. Kaczyński pledged no cuts to social programmes and said PiS would name heads of state firms and institutions in advance. Opinion: critics on the government side have not yet responded in the sources read.

items.notes: One poll; PiS at 15.5% is far below other recent polls — treat as single data point.
items.text: An IBRiS poll for Wirtualna Polska puts KO on 30.0% (+2.8), PiS 15.5% (−2.7), Konfederacja 14.0%, Braun's Konfederacja Korony Polskiej 9.1%, Lewica 6.8%, Morawiecki's Rozwój Plus 6.1%, PSL 4.5%, Razem 3.1% and Polska 2050 0.8%. Morawiecki says Rozwój Plus will run alone, not on a joint right-wing list.

PFR chief Mikołaj Raczyński told Rzeczpospolita that the state fund has up to 1 bn zł to take minority stakes in Polish firms expanding abroad, including acquisitions in Germany, Scandinavia and the US, and that this could grow to several billion. Three more state institutions are joining the Team Poland export-support group, to be named on Monday.
A Warsaw court ordered JFC Polska to remove material using an AI-generated imitation of narrator Jarosław Łukomski's voice and to pay more than 47,000 zł in damages; the ruling is not final.

Police detained a 57-year-old who phoned a Warsaw foundation referring to the Kraków attack and suggesting a similar one; he was charged with causing a false alarm (six months to eight years) and placed under police supervision.

The Małopolska voivode's office says nine people injured in the Nov 7 Main Square attack remain in five Kraków hospitals after another woman was discharged from the University Hospital. The attack killed six and injured 15, including two police officers.

Horse-drawn carriages returned to the Main Square on Saturday after a week's absence; the city reopened the permanent stand and the replacement stands. The drivers' association said they were going back to their place; carriage drivers and horses were among those hurt in the Nov 7 attack.

The 39-year-old who fired at police in Prokocim on Nov 12 was charged with actively assaulting officers, attempted coercion and drug possession; police say the gun was a CO2 air revolver. He had served a long sentence for murder and left prison at the end of 2025. Prosecutors asked for temporary arrest.

items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Only the contractor's side so far.
items.text: The city's sports infrastructure board (ZIS) abruptly ended the contracts of Krzysztof Czwartkiewicz, hired to commercialise the Wisła stadium. He blames officials and procedure for delays, says he never got a meeting with Gibała or his deputy, and claims the project could earn about 5m zł by end-2027 (contracts worth about 290,000 zł over two years). ZIS has not yet given its reasons.

Renovation of the Zielony Jar Wandy park amphitheatre (new roof, stage, seating, lighting, drainage; contract 748,000 zł with STAR-KOP Urbańczyk) is due to finish on Dec 18; the scope was cut to fit the budget.
First snow in Podhale caused trouble for lorries on hill climbs around Zakopane; a temporary church made of 250 tonnes of ice has been built on Hrebienok in the Slovak Tatras.

IMD's 05:30 IST bulletin on Nov 15 says the Bay of Bengal low has become a depression near 9.0°N 86.9°E, about 1,040 km SSE of Visakhapatnam and 1,160 km SSE of Gopalpur. It is expected to become Cyclonic Storm Akvan on Nov 16 and a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay on Nov 17, moving north-northwest. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh are recalling fishermen and readying shelters; Ganjam cancelled Sunday leave for staff. Landfall area not yet forecast. It would be the season's third cyclone after Arnab and Murasu.

items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Gandhi's figures are his claims, not verified. Visa refusals: Reported.
items.text: At the Telangana government's Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi claimed India stopped being a democracy in 2014, questioned the legitimacy of elections after roll revisions he said removed about 140 million voters, and repeated Maharashtra voter-addition allegations. BJP's CR Kesavan called it a "Bharat Badnaam Summit" and questioned foreign delegates' links; MEA said visa decisions are sovereign after reports that over 100 foreign invitees were refused or had visas revoked.

items.notes: Official PIB release not opened directly.
items.text: An MNRE factsheet puts installed power capacity at about 560 GW in October 2026, about 55% non-fossil, including roughly 175 GW solar and 59 GW wind; PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar has reached 65.26 lakh of its 1 crore household target.

Modi leaves for Manila on Nov 16 for three days for the India–ASEAN and East Asia summits, which Trump also attends. Sources tell ThePrint a US-hosted Quad leaders' summit is likely on Nov 17, the first in two years, but MEA calls it unconfirmed, and a formal Modi–Trump bilateral is unlikely if it happens. The White House has said on record that Trump will meet the Quad leaders.
